one_line: A mid-level Awadh talukdar’s son turned sepoy, caught between landlord interests, peasant grievances and the 1857–59 revolt.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s, lean but wiry, soldier’s posture with a landholder’s quiet confidence.
appearance.face: Oval face, warm medium-brown Awadhi complexion, sharp nose, defined jaw, neatly groomed moustache, thoughtful eyes with a steady, slightly wary gaze and a calm, determined default expression.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled back into a low knot at the back of the head, mostly hidden under a deep red turban tied in the mid-19th century North Indian style with a narrow golden-brown border; a small, plain steel khula top (metal cap) suggested beneath the cloth as structure but not prominently visible.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length off‑white cotton angarkha (cross‑tied wrap tunic) with side‑ties and a modest stand collar, over a pale yellow long‑sleeved kurta whose cuffs peek from the angarkha sleeves; around his waist is a broad indigo‑dyed cotton kamarband (sash) wrapped twice and knotted on his left, securing a simple brown leather pouch; his lower body is clad in straight, slightly loose churidar‑style trousers in earthy light brown, gathered neatly at the ankles, tucked into soft dark brown leather shoes with modestly upturned toes; over his shoulders sits a faded olive‑green cotton shawl, worn loosely like a rural chieftain’s chadar, with a subtle woven border in maroon and cream; his look mixes sepoy practicality and talukdar respectability, with textiles clearly hand‑woven, matte and unornate except for simple borders.
appearance.signature: A long, slightly weathered talwar with a brass hilt and disc‑pommel, carried sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard hanging from his left hip through his indigo kamarband, his right hand often resting lightly on the hilt to show his role as both soldier and landlord’s heir.

ref_desc: Raghav Singh is a lean late‑20s Awadh talukdar’s son with medium‑brown skin, moustache, deep red turban over black hair knot, off‑white angarkha, pale yellow kurta, indigo sash, brown churidar trousers, olive shawl and a brass‑hilt talwar at his hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Raghav Singh: a lean late‑20s Awadh man with medium‑brown skin, oval face, sharp nose, defined jaw and a neatly groomed moustache, his expression calm and determined. His thick black hair is pulled into a low knot mostly hidden beneath a deep red mid‑19th century North Indian turban with a narrow golden-brown border, suggesting a simple steel cap underneath as structure. He wears a knee-length off‑white cotton angarkha with cross ties and a modest stand collar over a pale yellow long‑sleeved kurta whose cuffs peek from the angarkha sleeves. Around his waist is a broad indigo cotton kamarband wrapped twice and knotted on his left, with a small brown leather pouch. His lower body has straight, slightly loose earthy light-brown churidar-style trousers gathered at the ankles, tucked into soft dark brown leather shoes with modestly upturned toes. A faded olive-green cotton shawl with a subtle maroon and cream woven border lies over his shoulders like a rural chieftain’s chadar. At his left hip hangs a long talwar in a dark brown leather scabbard, with a brass hilt and disc pommel, supported by the indigo sash, his right hand resting lightly on the hilt. Use off-white, indigo, olive green, deep red and earthy brown as the dominant colours and present him front-facing in a neutral stance so all costume details, turban, shawl and sword are clearly visible.
